'''Alexander Christopher Paseau''' is a British philosopher of Greek and Belgian origin. He is professor of mathematical philosophy at the [[University of Oxford]] and the Stuart Hampshire Fellow at [[Wadham College, Oxford|Wadham College]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alexander Paseau |url=https://www.philosophy.ox.ac.uk/people/alexander-paseau|website=University of Oxford|language=en}}</ref> He specialises in the [[philosophy of logic]], the [[philosophy of mathematics]], [[metaphysics]], [[epistemology]], and the [[philosophy of religion]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=A.c. Paseau (Oxford University) – PhilPeople |url=https://philpeople.org/profiles/a-c-paseau |website=Philpeople.org |language=en}}</ref>

As of January 2025, he is editor-in-chief of ''[[The Journal for the Philosophy of Mathematics]]''<ref>https://riviste.fupress.net/index.php/jpm/about/editorialTeam</ref>. He has been an Associate Editor of the journal ''[[Mind (journal)|Mind]]'' and has held Research Fellowships from the [[Mind Association]] and the [[Leverhulme Trust]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Research Fellowships 2019|url=https://www.leverhulme.ac.uk/research-fellowships-2019 |website=The Leverhulme Trust}}</ref>

==Research work==
Paseau subscribes to a broadly realist conception of mathematical truth, stating in an interview that "mathematical truth is not tensed. Mathematicians discover mathematical truths; they don’t make them up".<ref>{{Cite web |title=Along With The Eggs, Are There Sets Of Eggs In The Fridge Too? And Other Key Questions... |url=https://www.3-16am.co.uk/articles/along-with-the-eggs-are-there-sets-of-eggs-in-the-fridge-too-and-other-key-questions |access-date=2022-06-25 |website=3:16 |language=en}}</ref> In the same interview, Paseau also maintains that "inductive reasoning is crucial for mathematical knowledge" and that "we can know a mathematical truth without ever having proved it".

In their book ''One True Logic'', Paseau and his co-author Griffiths argue that there is one correct foundational logic and that it is highly [https://blogs.kent.ac.uk/thereasoner/files/2022/09/TheReasoner-167.pdf infinitary].

Paseau also works on the subtraction argument for metaphysical nihilism. Paseau's view is discussed and defended by [[Gonzalo Rodriguez-Pereyra]] in "The Subtraction Arguments for Metaphysical Nihilism: Compared and Defended".<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Puzzle of Existence: Why Is There Something Rather Than Nothing? |url=https://www.routledge.com/The-Puzzle-of-Existence-Why-Is-There-Something-Rather-Than-Nothing/Goldschmidt/p/book/9781138823440 |access-date=2022-06-25 |website=Routledge & CRC Press |language=en}}</ref>

==Books==
* ''Mathematical Knowledge'', co-editor with [[Mary Leng]] and Michael Potter, Oxford University Press 2007<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Chudnoff |first1=E. |title=Mathematical Knowledge, edited by Mary Leng, Alexander Paseau, and Michael Potter. |journal=Mind |date=1 July 2009 |volume=118 |issue=471 |pages=846–850 |doi=10.1093/mind/fzp079 |url=https://philpapers.org/rec/CHUMKE |language=en|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |title=Mathematical Knowledge |journal=Mathematical Association of America |url=https://maa.org/press/maa-reviews/mathematical-knowledge}}</ref>.
* ''Philosophy of Mathematics'', (ed.), 5 volumes, Routledge 2017.
* ''One True Logic'', with Owen Griffiths, Oxford University Press 2022<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Stei |first1=Erik |title=Review of One True Logic: A Monist Manifesto |date=17 October 2023 |url=https://ndpr.nd.edu/reviews/one-true-logic-a-monist-manifesto/ |language=en |issn=1538-1617|journal=Notre Dame Philosophical Reviews}}</ref>.
* ''Indispensability'', with [[Alan Baker (philosopher)|Alan Baker]], Cambridge University Press, 2023.
* ''The Euclidean Programme'', with Wesley Wrigley, Cambridge University Press, 2024.
* ''Propositional Logic'', MIT Press, forthcoming.
* ''What is Mathematics About?'', Oxford University Press, forthcoming.
